newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-THUGWANE OPTS OUT OF WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-THUGWANE OPTS OUT OF WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Olympic marathon champion Josiah Thugwane of South Africa announced on Monday that he would not be running at the world championships in Athens in August.

Thugwane, who became South Africa's first black Olympic gold medallist when he narrowly won the event in Atlanta, was speaking at a news conference to announce his participation at this year's London marathon on April 13.
"I will not run (in the world championships) because we have a lot of good runners in South Africa who also need the chance to represent the country internationally," he said.
Thugwane's decision was endorsed by another of South Africa's top marathon men, his training partner Lawrence Peu who also competed in Atlanta.
"We are trying to sell our country to the world," Peu said. "The best way to do that is to let other people represent South Africa as well."
The London marathon's international race co-ordinator Dave Bedford was delighted that Thugwane, who has raced only once since his Olympic triumph, has chosen to run in London.
"To get the Olympic champion...is going to add a great deal of interest to the race," he said.
"He's obviously a great runner and the fact that he was the first black South African to win an Olympic title means something to everyone around the world."

The London field has lost three-time winner Dionicio Ceron of Mexico but Thugwane still faces a high class field which will be led by Portugal's Antonio Pinto, Steve Moneghetti of Australia and top Britons Paul Evans, Eamonn Martin and Gary Staines.

The 25-year-old Thugwane is still recovering from a "road rage" attack in Johannesburg less than a fortnight ago, the second attack in a year. Before the Olympics he narrowly escaped death when he was assaulted and a bullet grazed his chin.
The latest incident, however, has not disrupted the former mineworker's training schedule.
"They wanted to injure my legs but another car came along and they ran away. But they hit me in the mouth and I still have pain there, sometimes it's difficult to eat."
Thugwane was due to visit a dentist in London before flying to Albuquerque in New Mexico to continue his training with Peu.
Peu was not originally due to run in London but was signed up by Bedford on Sunday night.
"It was in the Coach and Horses (pub) in Hampstead -- it's amazing what a couple of beers can do," laughed Bedford.
